final_content: {"summary":"Best-supported servo cause is gravity-driven linear velocity persisting across pose-only teleports, with collision/contact and scheduling modulating excursions. Frequency or offset alone cannot explain the pattern. DDS retry is conditionally useful but bounded by whether the server retained/resulted and whether failure is startup discovery or dropped response.","observations":["Gravity off + collision on: z exactly 0.1175 in all four cases, even with after_reply drops at 20 ms, so command transport failure alone is not sufficient to cause drift and target offset is not present in that condition.","Gravity on + collision on: z_max near target but below-threshold fractions 14-28%; non-monotonic across 0.1/0.02 s and after_reply/fixed_deadline, so simple frequency or constant offset does not explain data.","Gravity on + collision off: large falls; z_min from about -0.17 to -3.06 m; below fractions 73-93%. Velocity inference for two 0.1 s cases gives slope about -9.7/-9.8 m/s2 versus sim age and v to about -28 m/s, with one excellent and one moderate ballistic fit.","Source observation: WorldPoseCmd handler calls SetWorldPose, no SetWorldLinearVelocity in that block. Vendor commit not matched.","DDS: Cyclone natural goals showed 0 missed first/final responses; injected first-response drop recovered 4/4 by same-goal reread, all-response drop timed out 1/1. FastDDS natural UDP-only had 0 action-response misses but startup discovery failures and one client timeout; first-response injection recovered 4/4. No native stack, SHM claim not supported."],"assumptions":["Inferred velocity comes from position arcs, not a direct velocity topic.","Physics_dt and target_z are as given; cases are treated as separate probe runs, not necessarily identical seeds.","Installed vendor behavior may differ from the inspected upstream source block.","DDS evidence is two-process synthetic, isolated-domain, short-lived, constant 20 ms callback; not full robot pipeline.","Correction: lower RTF decreases simulation time between wall-time commands (wall interval x RTF), not increases it. It cannot by itself increase sim-time fall per wall command."],"conclusions":{"servo":"Primary attribution: pose-only teleport does not cancel linear velocity; gravity integrates it between commands, so velocity persists/accumulates. Collision contact modulates or intermittently arrests this. Frequency/scheduling can change inter-command sim gaps and sampling, but evidence is non-monotonic and gravity-off controls are exact, so frequency alone is insufficient. Offset alone is ruled out by exact gravity-off z and gravity-on z_max near target.","dds":"Retry is necessary only for specific transient losses, not globally. It is sufficient only when server accepted/executed and retained result, and the failure is a lost response the client can reread. It is not sufficient for all-response loss, pre-request startup discovery failure, result eviction, QoS mismatch, or timeout. Startup discovery failures must be separated from actual dropped results."},"ranked_hypotheses":[{"rank":1,"hypothesis":"SetWorldPose teleports pose without zeroing velocity; gravity causes velocity persistence/accumulation across resets, especially collision-free.","justification":"Directly supported by source block and inferred velocity slopes near -g with large negative v in collision-free 0.1 s cases."},{"rank":2,"hypothesis":"Contact solver interaction with teleporting poses causes below-threshold excursions when gravity is on, even if velocity is partly reset.","justification":"Gravity-on collision-on cases deviate but far less than collision-off; contact can arrest velocity or cause transient penetration/resolution."},{"rank":3,"hypothesis":"Schedule/drop-induced longer sim-time gaps alter fall depth but do not alone cause the pattern.","justification":"After_reply has variable intervals and drops; however gravity-off cases with drops remain exact, and below fractions are non-monotonic."},{"rank":4,"hypothesis":"Constant z offset/calibration error causes below-target readings.","justification":"Ruled out by gravity-off exact 0.1175 and gravity-on z_max near target."},{"rank":5,"hypothesis":"RTF/wall-time aliasing explains worse cases.","justification":"Lower RTF would reduce sim time per wall command, not increase fall; unless RTF varied, it cannot be primary. It remains a confound to measure."},{"rank":6,"hypothesis":"DDS transport loss directly drives servo drift.","justification":"Unlikely; gravity-off with drops is exact. It may perturb command timing only."}],"discriminating_experiments":[{"experiment":"Probe-only A/B: same partition/world, identical gravity/collision/period/schedule, patch only the pose command to zero linear/angular velocity after SetWorldPose or use a velocity-aware controller. Record direct linear velocity and each reset.","discriminates":"Hypothesis 1 vs contact/scheduling alternatives."},{"experiment":"Direct velocity instrumentation at command and reset times for 0.02 s cases, including collision-free. Compare whether frequent SetWorldPose clears velocity or only repositions it.","discriminates":"Frequency vs velocity persistence."},{"experiment":"Use sim-time-stamped commands at fixed sim intervals in probe, while logging RTF, and compare with wall-time 0.1/0.02 schedules.","discriminates":"RTF/wall-time aliasing and genuine period effects."},{"experiment":"Inject known z offsets in probe under gravity off/on to test whether offset alone reproduces below-threshold fractions.","discriminates":"Offset hypothesis."},{"experiment":"Benchmark-safe remedy test: duplicate benchmark world/protocol and apply remedy only as an overlay in that duplicate, not in original runtime. Pre-register probe metrics; only if probe normalizes, run duplicate benchmark and compare. Keep original world/protocol untouched.","discriminates":"Physical remedy efficacy without contaminating benchmark."},{"experiment":"DDS stage-instrumented two-process action: log discovery, node init, server wait, call, goal accept, execute, result send, client receive. Compare fixed domain/threads/launch, server-wait barrier, default vs UDP-only, native stack for SHM.","discriminates":"Startup discovery vs actual dropped result, and overlap confound."},{"experiment":"DDS deliberate drop matrix: first-response drop, result drop, all-response drop; test same-goal reread vs new goal, retry/backoff, reliable QoS.","discriminates":"Necessary/sufficient boundaries of retry."}],"falsifiers":["If zeroing velocity after SetWorldPose does not remove gravity-on drift, hypothesis 1 is false or insufficient.","If direct velocity is zero at resets in collision-free cases yet z still falls, velocity persistence is not supported.","If fixed sim-time commands reproduce the same non-monotonic below fractions, scheduling/wall-time aliasing is not primary.","If gravity-off cases with drops repeatably drift, transport/drop could suffice; current evidence contradicts.","DDS: If startup discovery failures persist after fixed domain/threads/launch and server-wait barrier, they are real discovery failures, not result loss. If same-goal reread recovers injected first-response drops but not all-response drops, retry sufficiency is bounded. If natural no-drop rates remain zero with retry disabled, retry is not necessary for baseline.","If FastDDS failures disappear only with UDP-only fixed setup but reappear with default/SHM/overlap, startup discovery/overlap is culprit, not action result loss."],"limitations":["Velocity inference exists for only two 0.1 s collision-free cases; no direct velocity topic or 0.02 s inference.","Vendor source not matched to immutable commit; source behavior may differ.","Servo probe is mechanism diagnostic, not benchmark; sampling about 150 points and wall-clock intervals can alias transients.","DDS evidence is synthetic, isolated-domain, short-lived, no native SHM stack, no host sleep/resume or network-interface change.","Budget and scope prevent full-pipeline generalization; absence of failure in these runs does not prove it never fails."]}
